paragraphs.text: Fallback model chain for DeepSeek Harness: when a model request keeps failing, the work continues on
the next model in your list.
# dsh-fallback-models
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that adds a fallback-model chain. When a model request still fails a
fter DSH uses up its own retries, work continues using the next model you listed instead of ending t
he turn with an error.
- An ordered list of fallback models (provider, model, and optionally reasoning effort), set globall

y and, if you like, per agent preset.
- Kicks in after DSH's retry plugin (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-ret

ry`) runs out of attempts, and only when a different model could plausibly fix the failure.
- For an

y one failure, each model gets at most one attempt, so loops cannot occur.
- By default, once the tu

rn needing the fallback ends, the session goes back to the model it started with.
- The conversation
shows a notice row, such as `deepseek/deepseek-chat failed (RATE_LIMIT); switched to openrouter/qwe

n3`.
- You can change it through model pickers from the plugin's settings page or in the profile con

figuration.
- An empty list, the default, leaves behavior unchanged.
## Installation
Install it straight from GitHub, adding it to a profile (`web` here):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
You can also use the Plugins page, or the plugin manager (`install_bundle` with `github:soffits/dsh-
fallback-models` or a local clone's path). Then open **Plugins > dsh-fallback-models** and press **C
onfigure** on the `fallback-models` row. Requirements are DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 or later in the 0.2.x serie
s and Node.js 22 or later.
## Configuration
The settings page lists models from DSH's catalog (the same set the model picker inside the composer
shows), so you can pick a provider, choose a model, and set a reasoning effort when the model suppo
rts one. Rows can be reordered. The same values live inside the profile patch attached to the plugin
. Rows can be reordered. The same values live inside the profile patch attached to the plugin's row:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `chain` | `[]` | Fallback models tried in order. An empty value disables the plugin. |
| `presets`
| `{}` | Maps a preset id to a separate list that overrides `chain` for agents in that preset. An e

mpty list turns fallback off for it. |
| `scope` | `turn` | `turn`: switch back to the model the ses
sion started with when the fallback-using turn ends. `session`: keep the fallback until the session

ends. |
| `codes` | see below | Failure codes that cause a switch to another model. |
All fields apply at the next failure; DSH does not need a restart.
### Failures that cause a switch
DSH's adapters report every failed request with a code independent of the provider. By default, thes
e codes cause a switch:
| Code | Meaning |
| `RATE_LIMIT`, `SERVER`, `TIMEOUT`, `TRANSPORT`, `EMPTY_RESPONSE` | Service overload, outage, slown

ess, or a broken connection. DSH retries these before any model switch. |
| `QUOTA`, `ACCOUNT_QUOTA`

| Balance or quota used up. DSH does not retry these, so the switch is immediate. |
| `PI_AI_ERROR`
| A provider error the pi-ai adapter failed to classify, for example a 404 for a withdrawn model. |
`AUTH` (rejected credentials), `INVALID_REQUEST`, and `CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED` (handled by DSH comp
action) do not switch models by default, because a model change would hide a problem you probably ne
ed to fix. To allow it anyway, include them in `codes` or tick them via the settings page. Cancelled
requests (`ABORTED`, or any turn you stopped) never switch.
This plugin sees only failures reported by the model request. When DSH hits an error while it prepar
es a request (a model id that does not exist, or a missing API key), nothing is sent, the turn ends,
and fallback does not happen.
## How it works
DSH's agent loop exposes one public route for recovering model requests: the `agent/request-error` w
aterfall (declared in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent`). `dsh-llm-retry` listens there; after its budget run
s out, or when it does not retry that kind of failure, it hands the failure to the next listener ("d
ownstream recovery"). This plugin is that next listener. Since it invokes `next()` first, DSH's retr
y and other recovery paths (context compaction, image offload) always get their turn, and it acts on
ly when nothing asked for a retry.
The model for a step is fixed before the step starts: a `retry` answer reruns that same provider/mod
el, and the 0.2.2 loop forbids changing models inside `agent/request`. DSH's documented way to chang
e models is calling `agent.model.select()` ahead of the next step. So the plugin does this:
1. picks the next listed model with a registered provider that DSH's LLM service will accept (`llm.r

esolveCallConfig`), skipping unusable entries;
2. makes it the model the session uses next through `
agent.model.select()` (a `model/selection` session event; the stored default model stays as it was);
3. closes the failed turn with a plugin cancel (`{ kind: 'hook' }`, keeping queued messages), recor

ding the reason on that turn's `turn/end` event;
4. queues a short notice message ahead of anything
you queued meanwhile, and that message launches the following turn using the fallback model.
The new turn sees the whole conversation (your latest message, any tool results, the plugin's notice
, and in the Web UI DSH's own `[model changed: ...]` note) and carries on. If the fallback fails too
, the next model goes through the same process. When the list runs out, the turn ends with the origi
nal error. With `scope: turn`, the session's starting model is reselected as soon as that continuati
on turn ends (unless you picked another model in between).
### What you see
- A notice row shows in the conversation: `<old model> failed (<code>); switched to <new model>`. Ex

panding it reveals the full text the model got.
- The turn that was interrupted is flagged as stoppe
d, and the session log stores this reason: `dsh-fallback-models: <old> failed (<code>); continuing o

n <new>`.
- While active, the fallback model appears in the composer picker.
- Host log entries tagg
ed `fallback-models` appear whenever a switch, skip, or restore happens.
### What reaches the model
Each switch produces one user-role notice, for example:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
DSH starts a turn only when input arrives, so this message starts the continuation; it also tells th
e model why its reply is starting over. The model sees nothing else from the plugin. Just like DSH's
own retries, the failed attempt stays invisible to the model.
